decisions.boundary_condition: Use a 3.5 minimum when the search is explicitly budget-focused. Apply either threshold only to the rating metric under discussion, and do not conflate hotel class, Google ratings, and customer-review ratings.
decisions.canonical_value: Use a soft 4.0 rating floor for nice, upscale, or resort-style hotel searches and a soft 3.5 rating floor for explicitly budget-focused searches, applied to the rating metric stated in context.
decisions.condition: When a hotel search calls for a well-rated property and frames the stay as nice, upscale, resort-style, or explicitly budget-focused.
decisions.default_action: Filter or prioritize options meeting a 4.0 minimum for nice, upscale, or resort-style searches, and identify the rating source when known.
decisions.exception_condition: Follow any newly stated threshold or metric. If no suitable option meets the applicable floor while satisfying more important trip constraints, ask before relaxing it.
decisions.name: contextual_hotel_rating_floor
decisions.preference_value: Prefer hotels rated at least 4.0 when seeking a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay; for explicitly budget-focused searches, prefer at least 3.5.
decisions.rationale: The four-star policy is the well-supported upscale/nice branch of the contextual rating-floor policy, with overlapping evidence, while the 3.5 threshold is a distinct budget fallback. Merging preserves one conditional policy without promoting 4.0 to a universal hard requirement or conflating hotel class with review-rating metrics.
